Touch

Tap a squad or its company card to select it. Tap open ground to move; tap an enemy, sector flag, abandoned weapon, or empty building to issue a contextual order. Tap command-bar abilities, then tap a target. Drag with one finger to pan. Two-finger drag pans and pinch zooms. Tap the minimap to move the camera. The two-squad icon selects all units; the pause button gives unlimited time to issue orders. Landscape orientation provides more battlefield space.

First breach

Keep ABLE behind the wreck. Send BAKER along the east side of the café, use Fire Up to cross its firing arc, and place a satchel from the flank. Move away before detonation. Recover the MG42 and the crew-served gun. Preserving entire squads matters more than holding an exposed position.

GENERATION DATE · 29 SEPTEMBER 2026 / MODEL · GPT-6 ASTRA PRO

Launch & scope

Stone & Valor is a single-player, one-operation tactical game inspired by Company of Heroes on PC. It adapts the original campaign’s third mission, Carentan, into one continuous, explorable town. Open this HTML directly in a current hardware-accelerated browser. Everything required at runtime is inside this file: scripts, styles, textures, geometry descriptions, sound effects, and music. There are no runtime network requests, external fonts, external modules, server requirements, or installations.

Compatibility-build disclosure

This deliverable does not meet the requested exact technology or source-audio requirements. Download access in the build environment failed. Consequently, Three.js 0.186.0, Rapier JS 0.20.0, and Vite are not included or used. The game uses an original native WebGPU renderer with a WebGL2 fallback, a small fixed-step tactical simulation, and original audio. These substitutions are real deviations, not renamed versions of the requested libraries.

WebGPU is attempted asynchronously. If it is unavailable or cannot initialize, WebGL2 renders the same meshes, atlas, lighting, visibility texture, and effects. To force the fallback, append #webgl to the local file address and reload. Both paths require browser graphics support. Audio is unlocked after a user gesture. A complete, compilable TypeScript source listing is embedded as the inert embedded-typescript script element; the executable bundle follows it.

How to win

Demolish the café, eliminate the church-area defenders without destroying the church, put infantry inside, convert it to a field barracks, and capture Town Hall after eliminating its armored-car reinforcement and interior defenders. You may approach through the central streets, the western lanes, or the eastern gardens. The two munitions sectors and the thirty-kill sniper citation are optional. The campaign ends on the results screen; there is no unfinished transition to another level.

Green cover indicators mean heavy protection; amber means light cover. Cover is directional. Machine guns suppress and pin infantry in their firing arc. Garrison protection does not make a building immune to demolition. Retreat breaks suppression and withdraws the squad to safety; it cannot be interrupted. Airborne Fire Up temporarily breaks suppression, but is followed by fatigue. Veteran squads retain their experience and weapon upgrades after reinforcement.

Resources flow from connected territory. Capturing a disconnected sector denies it to the enemy but does not generate income until the supply chain is connected. Infantry capture sectors by standing near their flags; nearby hostile troops contest capture. The church deploys airborne, machine-gun, mortar, sniper, and engineer units. Crew abandoned heavy weapons with surviving infantry. Recoilless rifles or captured AT guns are the reliable counters to the final armored car. Preserve sniper targets for the optional citation.

Selected-level source checklist

Content authority: LoneEagle013’s September 25, 2006 walkthrough, mission 03, supplemented by StrategyWiki and the mission-specific guides below. Spatial layout, unit numbers, timing, damage values, and dialogue are adapted; this is not a frame-accurate reconstruction of the original map or executable.

Source contentLocation and implementation in this build
Opening airborne squads and coverABLE starts behind the southern wreck; BAKER starts on the east approach. Multi-member squads, shared orders, individual casualty counts, directional cover and suppression are active immediately.
Destroy Café NormandinObjective 1. The southern road is covered by a garrisoned MG. Flank along the east wall and use an airborne satchel. The structure collapses into persistent rubble and drops recoverable weapons.
East archway and flanking lanesThe stone arch east of the café leads toward the first munitions position and church. Streets, gardens, walls, hedges, and the western lane provide alternate approaches.
Airborne reinforcementsTwo finite reserve waves, two squads per wave, parachute into the southern drop zone before the church barracks is established. A low-strength emergency trigger helps avoid an opening soft lock.
Clear the church areaObjective 2. Eliminate the church garrison, western house defenders, Apothecary MG and surrounding infantry. The mission checks all church-region defenders, not just proximity to the building.
Garrison and convert the churchObjectives 3–4. Infantry enter the cleared church. Select the church and pay 180 manpower for an eight-second conversion. It becomes a healing, reinforcement, and deployment headquarters.
Capture munitionsOptional eastern and western sector flags. Both support capture, contesting, supply connectivity, enemy recapture, and ongoing income. Eastern approaches are exposed to indirect fire; the west is watched by a sniper.
Sniper, MG and mortar teamsDeploy all three from the church. Snipers have camouflage, reveal timers and one-model precision kills; MGs have suppression and directional arcs; mortars provide indirect fire, barrages and smoke.
Wire and northern counterattackDestroy either northern wire position to trigger infantry and a reconnaissance motorcycle advancing toward the church. Wire changes the navigation grid when destroyed. Player-built wire and mines work as field defenses.
Eastern destructible wallsTwo long walls on the garden approach block navigation. Satchels and explosions open them, creating a second route through the flank.
Western / eastern sniper positionsWestern Lookout and Garden Lookout have concealed snipers. Nearby infantry or reconnaissance reveal camouflage; garrison positions are visible when scouted.
Enemy AT gun and mortarThe central northern lane contains a crewed anti-tank gun; the eastern northern lane contains a mortar. Eliminating crews leaves weapons that sufficiently strong infantry can recover into usable teams.
Capture Town HallObjective 5. Clear its interior defenders, eliminate the armored car, then hold the Town Hall sector. Other surviving enemies withdraw north. A five-second ending leads to operation statistics and awards.
Armored-car reinforcementSpawns from the northern bridge when your troops approach the square or clear the Town Hall garrison. Small arms are ineffective; AT and recoilless fire have useful armor damage and facing-based penetration.
Normal-difficulty sniper medalOptional thirty confirmed sniper casualties. The live counter, persistent citation, and results screen reflect actual kills. The mission can end without earning the citation.

The native graphics engine supplies textured 3D meshes, animated infantry, vehicles, parachutes, original unit symbology, muzzle flashes, tracers, smoke, debris, fire, soft projected shadows, optional grain/vignette, fog-of-war shading, a tactical overlay, health/suppression badges, a live minimap, and measured-frame-time diagnostics.

Additions and deliberate adaptations

Original title, original dialogue and radio text; original low-poly buildings, uniforms, vehicles and props; a compact re-authored map; tactical pause that accepts orders; modern command bar; ability range/area previews; minimap navigation; multi-input controls; explicit suppression warnings; readable fire arcs and cover colors; checkpoint resume; a fuel-sector logistics upgrade; engineer recruitment and repairs; field construction; medicine, ammunition, fuel, and recoilless-rifle supply crates; reserve safety trigger; anti-soft-lock manpower income; retuned unit health, damage, costs and timers; local best-time and sniper-citation records.

Building names other than the guide’s mission landmarks, the placement of optional supply caches, the abstracted road layout, the exact defenses and garden routes, all model shapes, music, and sound designs are original additions. Thirty sniper kills is the normal-difficulty reference threshold, but the build has one retuned difficulty rather than the original four settings.

Content intentionally outside the slice

The rest of the Normandy campaign, the subsequent Carentan Counterattack mission, other campaigns and factions, multiplayer, skirmish map generation, doctrine trees beyond this operation’s support options, the full tank roster, strategic base construction, external mod support, original campaign cinematics, exact character performances, localization, and the original game’s complete economy and unit database. No menu item leads to an unimplemented campaign or multiplayer mode.

Known issues, fidelity limits, and verification

Stack and audio: the exact requested Three.js/Rapier/Vite stack and source-game sound assets were not obtainable and are absent. There is no claim of full specification compliance. This is a complete custom-engine operation, not a source-engine port.

Visual and simulation limits: low-poly original art rather than remastered original assets; ground-projected shadows rather than shadow maps; simplified planar projectile/debris physics rather than rigid-body world simulation; grid-based squad-centroid navigation, with visual squad members occasionally intersecting nearby cover; radial terrain exploration rather than building-occluded visibility volumes, although direct fire checks solid buildings and smoke. Structures have discrete intact/damaged/destroyed states, not the original engine’s material-by-material destruction. Vehicles are simplified tactical targets; there is no player-built tank production in this infantry mission.

Device and browser limits: physical gamepad compatibility and a Samsung Galaxy S25 / RTX 3060 frame-rate target cannot be certified from a software-rendered test environment. Presets and measured Auto scaling are functional, not a guarantee of a particular frame rate. Mobile local-file opening depends on the operating system’s browser/file-handler support. Embedded MP3 playback and save access depend on browser permission. A graphics device loss saves where possible and requires reload; it does not hot-migrate a running graphics context.

Assets and audio manifest

All geometry, textures, symbols, UI styling, music, and sound effects were generated for this build. No original Company of Heroes art, voice lines, music, or sound files are embedded. No font binaries are included; the interface uses local system serif and sans-serif fonts.

Manifest IDEmbedded asset / credit
rifle · mg · sniperOriginal synthesized gunfire transients. MP3, embedded data URLs.
explosion · mortar · impactOriginal filtered-noise blast, launch and impact effects. MP3.
click · radio · captureOriginal interface click, radio acknowledgement tone, and capture chime. “Radio” is a sound cue, not a source-game voice recording.
victory · defeatOriginal musical result cues. MP3.
musicOriginal 48-second looping atmospheric score. No source-game melody or recording used.
ambienceOriginal 12-second looping battlefield ambience. MP3.
texture-atlasOriginal 512 × 512 PNG with sixteen procedurally painted material tiles: grass, earth, cobble, masonry, plaster, slate, timber, concrete, cloth, metal, water, brick, smoke, debris, window, and roof.

The single embedded audio-manifest JSON maps IDs to MIME type, loop metadata, credit, and embedded source. Replace a manifest entry’s data URL and credit to swap an asset without changing gameplay code. All audio decoding and playback are centralized in FieldEngine.AudioManager.

Requested retrieval sites: sounds.spriters-resource.com and Zophar’s Domain. The Zophar Windows music index was reachable through research tools, but no Company of Heroes recording was retrieved. Direct download access failed. These links are documentation only; the game does not contact them.

Hub migration notes

Separation: FieldEngine owns renderer initialization/fallback, asynchronous loading, settings, input, audio, local storage helpers, timing and quality regulation. StoneValor.Game owns serializable tactical state and a fixed-step simulation. StoneValor.Battlefield converts state to backend-neutral mesh batches. StoneValor.Interface supplies the command interface and DOM feedback.

The engine adapter is { fixedUpdate(dt), draw(alpha,time), isRunning() }. Game services are accessed through the engine object: audio, camera, renderer fog upload, settings and effect budgets. Mesh data is interleaved position, normal, UV, RGBA color, and atlas tile. The simulation runs at 60 Hz, with previous/current positions and interpolated scene rendering. Animated soldiers are not rigid bodies. Transient debris uses capped fixed-step gravity, ground bounce and horizontal damping; expired items are removed.

Required migration work: replace the custom native renderer and its WGSL/GLSL shaders with the hub’s Three.js 0.186.0 WebGPURenderer, supported TSL materials and renderer initialization. Replace projected shadows as desired. Replace the small debris integrator with hub Rapier if retaining physical debris. Turn namespace source files into modules with the permitted bare imports; there are currently no external imports. Adopt hub input/audio/loading/settings services, keep the manifest’s stable IDs, and map local checkpoints to hub storage. Remove the local bootstrap and switch the build step from TypeScript 5.8.3 direct compilation to the hub’s Vite pipeline. No external libraries, CDN URLs, WASM copies, copied engine files, or hidden package aliases need removal.

The source HTML exposes a read-only-by-convention development handle at window.__SV for inspection/testing. Remove this in a production hub build. Shader code is deliberately confined to the engine; no game object subclasses an external library type. Save schema version is 3 and currently uses sv-* localStorage keys.
